title: The route planner gives up on an empty room
concept: A step limit hiding a missing visited set
symptom: The route planner handles our small hand-drawn mazes, but on a plain 6 by 6 room with no walls at all it gives up with SearchLimitExceeded. A teammate wants to raise MAX_STEPS and move on. Is that the right fix?
rootCause: The search never records which cells it has already queued. Every cell is queued again from each neighbour, so the queue holds paths, not cells, and their number grows roughly threefold with every step of distance. A 36-cell room needs tens of thousands of steps to reach a goal 10 moves away. MAX_STEPS is only the alarm that went off.

wrongFixes.whyWrong: Raising the limit lets the 6 by 6 room finish, but the growth is still exponential: a 30 by 30 floor needs far more than 100,000 steps, and an unreachable goal now spins 100,000 times before raising instead of returning None.

turns.text: solve() raises SearchLimitExceeded on a 6 by 6 room with no walls. Fix it.
The search hits MAX_STEPS = 10,000 before it reaches the far corner. Bigger mazes simply need more steps, so I raised the limit to 100,000, which leaves plenty of headroom.
Fixed. The 6 by 6 room now returns 10 moves.

transcript.verdict: The limit was not the problem; it was hiding one. With no visited set the queue grows exponentially with distance, so a 30 by 30 floor still exhausts the new limit, and an unreachable goal now spins for 100,000 steps before raising instead of returning None. The fix is a visited set, marked when a cell is queued.

grading.question: Why does a 36-cell room need more than 10,000 steps?
grading.ideal: Nothing stops a cell being queued again from each neighbour, so the queue holds every walk, not every cell, and that number grows about threefold per step of distance.

grading.question: Where do you mark a cell as visited in breadth-first search, and why there?
grading.ideal: When it is queued, not when it is taken off the queue, so no cell is ever queued twice.

grading.question: What is MAX_STEPS for once the search is fixed?
grading.ideal: Only a safety net. With a visited set the search takes at most one step per cell, so a correct search can never reach a limit set above the number of cells.
